items.subject: New Electrical Meter Mains - Insufficient Clearance
items.question:
Current field-verified available area for the added electric meters is 50" wide. The proposed installation of (2) 400-amp meter mains and the associated wireway requires approximately 7'-0" of clear width to accommodate the equipment per code and manufacturer working-clearance requirements.

Please advise how the design team would like to proceed, given the discrepancy between the available field condition and the space required for the proposed equipment. Specifically:

1. Can the meter room/wall area be revised or expanded to provide the required 7'-0" of clearance?
2. If not, is an alternate meter configuration (e.g., different meter main arrangement, relocated wireway routing, or a different equipment layout) acceptable to fit within the 40" available?
3. Please confirm any impact to adjacent walls, structure, or utility coordination (SCE) resulting from either option.

items.subject: Basement Scope and MDF Room
items.question:

•  A000 key plan shows the basement area of work as 641 SF, but the A000 Project Information block still reads "Basement 913 SF."
•  A000 no longer lists basement improvements under a separate permit.
•  A090 still notes "Basement is existing to remain; no change," but the set adds new MDF room 00-02 with 1-hour C3 walls (A090, A110), a 45-minute door with card reader (A750), fire-treated plywood (A110 KN 5), and power and data (A130).
•  The A100 area-of-work boundary appears unchanged from the 8/28 set.
Per RFI-03, basement work was limited to the BOH items shown on the progress set (Panel PB, BOH partitions, FRP, sprinkler adjustments). Please confirm:
(a) The basement area of work, and which square footage governs.
(b) Whether MDF 00-02 is part of this TI permit and the Phase 2 scope.
(c) MDF requirements for dedicated cooling, grounding and bonding, and any fire suppression beyond the standard sprinkler system.

items.subject: Appliance Selection
items.question:
Carbon Fiber Cabinets is completing millwork shop drawings and needs the final appliance selections before drawing elevations. If the appliances change after the elevations are drawn, the casework will have to be redesigned and the schedule will slip. RFI-48 said Rapt would confirm appliance specs during this week’s coffee bar review with Intuit. Please provide the following:

(a) The final appliance schedule for the L1 Pantry/Coffee Bar and the basement BOH Pantry Support. For each appliance, list the manufacturer, model, finish and overall dimensions (W x D x H). This includes the AP04 Eversys C’2ms espresso machine and the milk fridge proposed in RFI-48, plus any refrigerator, microwave, ice machine, dishwasher, water heater or water filtration unit.

(b) Whether the Intuit Design Intent standard items (Nespresso Momento 100 coffee machine, GE microwave 6309842, Coswar 6564544 mini fridge) still apply or are replaced by the A810 schedule.

(c) How each appliance is installed: built-in, undercounter, countertop or freestanding. Please also confirm whether any units are panel-ready and need millwork fronts.

(d) The manufacturer’s required clearances for each appliance, including ventilation and airflow gaps, door swing and service access. Also list any countertop cutouts or grommets needed for water lines, drains or power.

(e) Furnished-by and installed-by responsibility for each appliance (Intuit/Compass or GC).

(f) Whether the millwork needs to accommodate the Day 2 commercial fridge placeholder shown at BOH, or whether the Day 1 millwork should be designed without it.

Please attach manufacturer cut sheets or installation guides for each selected appliance.

items.subject: Barn Door Specs
items.question:
We are pricing the curved wood barn doors. The current information says “painted” but doesn’t give a substrate or finish. Please confirm:

1. Wood species / substrate: What species or substrate should the curved doors be built from? Is paint-grade acceptable, such as poplar, maple or fire-retardant MDF (Medite FR or equal, the same as the brand-standard trim)?
2. Paint color and sheen: What paint color (manufacturer and number) and sheen (matte, eggshell, satin, semi-gloss, high gloss) do you want? The retail standards call for semi-gloss on doors and frames, painted PT-01. Please confirm that applies to the barn doors or give the intended finish.

items.subject: Rooftop Condensing Unit Support, Seismic Anchorage & Roof Framing Capacity
items.question:
The drawings don’t include a support or anchorage detail for these units, and no structural sheets were issued with the 95% set. M300 directs the contractor to “verify location of air handling unit, condensing unit and existing roof framing conditions and provide any new framing required to support equipment.” Please confirm the following:

Roof framing capacity: Can the existing roof framing support CU-1, CU-2 and CU-3 at the locations on M102, including seismic loads? If reinforcement or new support framing is required, please provide the design.
Support type: Please confirm the required support method for the condensing units (equipment rails, sleepers or a steel support frame), including minimum height above the roof surface and attachment to the roof structure. The refrigerant line penetration will use the weatherproof pipe curb per M102 keynote 1.
Indoor AHU supports: Please confirm the existing structure can carry the suspended AHUs, including the units stacked above the Level 2 restroom ceiling (M101 keynote 15), and identify any required supplemental framing.
Seismic anchorage: Please confirm whether seismic anchorage of the condensing units and AHUs will be handled as a deferred submittal (stamped calcs by the installing contractor’s engineer). If so, please add it to the deferred submittal list on the drawings so it can go through plan check.
items.nextAction: Assign a reviewer and record the next action.

items.subject: Acoustibuilt Substitution
items.question:
We are requesting review and approval for a proposed equal product substitution for the specified Armstrong Acoustibuilt system.

The proposed alternative system is “FADE”, manufactured by Ecophon (a division of CertainTeed).

2. Technical Specifications & Performance
Acoustical Performance: The proposed FADE system features an NRC rating of 0.80, meeting equal acoustical performance standards.

Coverage: Accurate acoustical plaster coverage per system specifications.

Maintainability & Patchability: The FADE system is repairable and patchable, allowing localized repairs without requiring large area replacement to fix small damaged spots.

3. Attachments & Supporting Documentation
Ecophon / CertainTeed FADE Technical Data Sheets & Product Documentation

4. No cost imapct
